utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Please be seated. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour, good morning everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-95-13/1-A, The Prosecutor versus Mile Mrksic and Veselin Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Let me first make sure that the audio equipment is working properly. Mr. Mrksic, can you hear me? THE ACCUSED MRKSIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. What about counsel for the Defence, can you all hear me?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, we hear you. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Counsel for the Prosecution, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: MR. DALAL
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And I'm not sure if I --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: You're not sure if you can what?

utterances.speaker: MR. DALAL
utterances.text: I'm not sure if I can hear the translation though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Translation, can we hear a good morning from you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Testing, testing, 1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: So that's all ready.

utterances.speaker: MR. DALAL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Appearances, please, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. DALAL
utterances.text: For the Prosecution today Marwan Dalal and with me is our case manager Mr. Sebastian van Hooydonk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dalal. For Mr. Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. The Defence of Mr. Mrksic today will be represented by Miroslav Vasic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vasic. For Mr. Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Good morning to all parties in the courtroom. I'm Novak Lukic. I represent Mr. Sljivancanin together with Mr. William St-Michel who will be assisting us in the appeals phase of the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. As you are aware, Rule 65 bis (B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence requires that Status Conferences be held every 120 days for each appellant in the Tribunal's custody. This Status Conference serves two primary purposes, first it allows the appellant an opportunity to express concerns relating to his appeal or detention conditions. Second, it provides an opportunity to update the appellants with respect to the status of their case. The Status Conference is also an opportunity for the Tribunal to inquire about the mental and physical condition of the detained person. The last Status Conference in this case took place on the 19th of February, 2008. While Mr. Mrksic is presently in custody of the Tribunal's detention unit, Mr. Sljivancanin is currently on provisional release, pursuant to a decision issued by the Appeals Chamber on 11 December 2007. I would like to begin this Status Conference by inquiring into Mr. Mrksic's case, Mr. Mrksic's health. Mr. Mrksic. THE ACCUSED MRKSIC: [Interpretation] Thank you for asking, Your Honour. I have no problems regarding my health or the detention unit. Well, the situation with my health is well known but it is not getting worse. Your Honours, for now, I don't have any problems. The situation in the detention unit is usual, as it has been for the past seven years. It is normal. As for my health, after two heart surgeries, thank God, at the moment, I'm feeling fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mrksic. And I'm glad to hear that you are well and that there are no special problems which we need to discuss on your conditions of health or conditions of detention. Mr. Vasic, do you have anything to add to that? Regarding the state of health.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. No, I have nothing to add. You have heard Mr. Mrksic and I think everything is fine and proceeding according to plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, I would like to use this opportunity to share with you some data on the development of the case and its preparation for the hearing. On 14 December 2007, I granted, in part, a joint Defence motion seeking an extension of time to file the appeal briefs. The Defence was ordered to file their appeal briefs 40 days following receipt of the official translation of the trial judgement into the B/C/S language and their responses to the Prosecution's appeal brief 20 days following the receipt of that translation. The Prosecution filed its confidential appeal brief on 14 January 2008 and the public version of its brief on 8 February 2008. I understand that the official B/C/S translation of the trial judgement was filed and distributed electronically to counsel for the Defence on 29 May 2008. Accordingly, the time-lines for the briefing schedule appear to be as follows with respect to the Prosecution's appeal. The Defence respondent's briefs were due yesterday, 18 June 2008. I know we have just received the respondent's brief of Mr. Mrksic. I have not yet received an official word from the registry about the status of Mr. Sljivancanin's brief. Counsel, would you tell us what is the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We submitted our brief last night around 10.00 p.m., so still within the deadline and then probably in the course of today you will receive our brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Well, thank you, Mr. Lukic, and I'm pleased so see that both defendants have submitted their briefs on time. Now the Prosecution's brief in reply are due, therefore, on the 3rd of July, 2008. Regarding the appeals by the Defence, the Defence appeal briefs are due on 8 July 2008. Again, assuming that the Defence briefs are not early, the Prosecution's respondent's briefs are due on 18 of August, 2008. And finally the Defence briefs in reply would be due on the 2nd of September 2008. I take this opportunity to remind the parties that their briefs should be filed in compliance with the practice direction on the length of briefs and motions and the practice direction on formal requirements for appeals from judgement. After the briefing schedule is complete the Appeals Chamber will schedule an appeal hearing in due course. My hope is that we will be able to have the hearing before the winter recess. At this point I would like to ask the parties whether they have any other issues that they would like to raise at this time. Mr. Dalal.

utterances.speaker: MR. DALAL
utterances.text: The Prosecution has nothing.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please for the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DALAL
utterances.text: The Prosecution has nothing to raise at this stage, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Vasic, regarding any issues on behalf of Mr. Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have a question regarding the submission, according to Rule 68 we received from our colleagues their submission yesterday that we were given material from a different case that also relates to Vukovar and that could be of significant for the Defence in this case. We actually received the material along with this submission, but my question is that it seems to me that this seems to be happening from one Status Conference to the next. Between the Status Conferences we haven't received any new material. So I would just like to ask my colleagues from the Prosecution to be a little more diligent in this matter so that perhaps we could receive any mitigating material in a timely fashion, in accordance to Rule 116. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: The Prosecution, would you comment on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DALAL
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, the Prosecution would like to emphasise that this is not necessarily material relevant to Rule 68, exculpatory material rather material under Rule 66. This is ongoing obligation, in accordance with a ongoing obligation of the Prosecution to disclose material and the Prosecution, we thought this is the most efficient way to disclose material that -- relevant to the Defence, witnesses that are come on in this trial and the Mrksic trial. Whenever we have several witnesses who have testified before the Mrksic trial and who have testified in the Seselj trial, we compile them and produce this material which is relevant and not exculpatory. Of course, if we discover something that is exculpatory, we would disclose it immediately to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, and I thank my colleague. I would just prefer this to be more prompt and to be ongoing because I see that we have testimonies here from March and now it's June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vasic, I really think that to the extent that you can, you should pass on these materials to the Defence whenever you can and as soon as you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. DALAL
utterances.text: The Prosecution agree with this approach. We would not have any problem to do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Okay. So let's hope that this will not be a problem in the future. Thank you. Any issues to raise on behalf of Mr. Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, but I would like to use this opportunity to inform you personally, since I was not present at the previous Status Conference and was not essential for me to be there, I would just like to inform that you the state of health of Mr. Sljivancanin is good, that I am in daily meetings with him at the appeal stage of the proceedings and that he completely adheres to all the instructions of the Court regarding the terms of his provisional release.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. I'm pleased to hear that. Since there are no other matters to be raised, let me thank the parties and the staff and the interpreters, the registrar and the parties, I thank you particularly for your attendance. And I call the proceedings to a close. The Court will now rise.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
